section_name: Evaluation Dependencies and Held-Out Validation in Parameter Correction

candidates.title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
candidates.reason: Provides a comprehensive framework distinguishing calibration-in-the-large (the estimated intercept) evaluated on estimation cohorts from validation on separate observations, showing that apparent zero error on the estimation set provides no evidence of true calibration.

candidates.title: A closed testing procedure to select an appropriate method for updating prediction models
candidates.reason: Investigates updating statistical predictors specifically via intercept recalibration and demonstrates why assessing model performance on the updating sample cannot substitute for validation on independent observations.

candidates.title: A calibration hierarchy for risk models was defined: from bad to good to extreme
candidates.reason: Defines mean calibration (intercept matching) and details how estimating an adjustment term and evaluating it on the exact same data produces trivially perfect apparent calibration without measuring out-of-sample performance.

candidates.title: How Biased is the Apparent Error Rate of a Prediction Rule?
candidates.reason: Foundational mathematical analysis demonstrating that evaluating error on the identical observations used to fit parameters creates an evaluation dependency that underestimates true prediction error.

candidates.title: The Estimation of Prediction Error: Covariance Penalties and Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Formulates covariance penalties between predictions and outcomes when parameters (such as intercepts) are estimated in-sample, demonstrating why in-sample evaluation yields no measurement of generalization to separate observations.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: The seminal paper establishing the methodological necessity of strictly separating the observations used to estimate predictor parameters from those used to evaluate prediction performance.

candidates.title: Internal and external validation of predictive models: a simulation study of bias and precision in small samples
candidates.reason: Demonstrates through simulation that evaluating fitted models on small development samples produces optimistic apparent performance that fails to reflect behavior on held-out or external samples.

candidates.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
candidates.reason: Analyzes the statistical dependency introduced when parameters or offsets are evaluated on the data used to estimate them, explaining why held-out test data is necessary to measure true error.

candidates.title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection
candidates.reason: Highlights that performing estimation or tuning steps without isolating held-out evaluation observations yields artificially low or zero apparent error, masking true prediction error.

candidates.title: A survey of cross-validation procedures for model selection
candidates.reason: Provides a comprehensive survey analyzing the mathematical divergence between apparent empirical risk on estimation samples and true risk on independent, held-out observations.

candidates.title: Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD): Explanation and Elaboration
candidates.reason: Establishes authoritative methodological reporting standards clarifying the distinction between apparent performance on development data and genuine performance on independent validation cohorts.

candidates.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in Machine-Learning-Based Science
candidates.reason: Examines pervasive data leakage and evaluation failure modes where post-hoc parameter corrections fitted on evaluation data invalidate claims of out-of-sample generalization.

candidates.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
candidates.reason: Demonstrates that post-hoc intercept and temperature adjustments must be strictly evaluated on separate held-out datasets to avoid trivial apparent calibration.
